channel.title: Daniel Scheidemantel Camargo — Writing
channel.description: Notes on applied AI engineering, cloud architecture and running systems in production.

item.title: End to end: why small companies can’t afford handoffs
item.description: A large company passes a feature through five pairs of hands; a small one usually has one. What that person needs most is the ability to carry a problem from the user's need through to years of maintenance.

item.title: AI is an accelerator, not a decision-maker
item.description: I build a platform that runs AI agents in production, so I have every commercial reason to say they're close to autonomous. They aren't, and I don't think a bigger model changes that.

item.title: You have to be bad at something again
item.description: Competence feels good, and it's often where learning stops. Moving country showed me which of my habits were only defaults, and you can get the same jolt without a plane ticket.

item.title: Planning a legacy migration: the rollout is the hard part
item.description: Writing the new system is the part you can estimate. Moving real traffic and real people onto it is where migrations fail, and it's usually the part planned last.
